title: Father of Glory, to Thy Name
description: Father of Glory, to Thy Name in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 267.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther of glo-ry, to Thy name Im-mor-tal praise we give, Who dost an act of grace pro-claim And bid us re-bels live.

lines: Father of glory, to Thy name
Immortal praise we give,
Who dost an act of grace proclaim
And bid us rebels live.
Immortal honor to the Son,
Who makes Thine anger cease;
Our lives He ransomed with His own
And died to make our peace.
To Thine almighty Spirit be
Immortal glory given,
Whose teachings bring us near to Thee
And train us up for heaven.
Let men with their united voice
Adore th’ eternal God
And spread His honors and their joys
Through nations far abroad.
Let faith and love and duty join
One grateful song to raise;
Let saints in earth and heaven combine
In harmony and praise.

licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
